## Outcome

Positive `panel.margin` support merged, and I made substantial implementation and test contributions to the collaborative `coord_equal` branch.

## Context

The panel-margin branch began before GSoC. During Week 10, I completed its review changes and merge. PR #253 is owned by `tdhock`; my work is recorded as a collaborative contribution rather than an authored PR.

## What I Did

- Merged [PR #286](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/286) on July 29.
- Contributed to [PR #253](https://github.com/animint/animint2/pull/253):
  - fixed scale-to-fit behavior for non-square viewports;
  - preserved data aspect ratio while using available panel space;
  - removed an R normalization that squared the aspect effect;
  - added a non-square viewport test;
  - added a y-axis-height case with `coord_fixed(10)`;
  - clarified NEWS and width/height cases.
- Synchronized the long-running facet-strip branch with changed main-branch text behavior.

## Learnings

`coord_equal` is not only a one-to-one unit relationship. The renderer must preserve the data ratio and choose the largest panel that fits a wide, tall, or faceted viewport.

## Challenges / Notes

Floating-point SVG coordinates made exact assertions brittle. The test needed enough tolerance for roughly 0.001 rendering noise without hiding a real aspect-ratio error.

## Next Week Targets

Run broad verification across the open renderer branches and prepare the final feature push.

<iframe src="week10-panel-margin-demo/index.html" title="Three Animint facet plots comparing zero, one, and two lines of panel margin" loading="lazy"></iframe>
:::

The three plots use identical Iris data. Only `panel.margin` changes, so the increasing space between facet panels is directly visible.

<details class="demo-code">
<summary>View the essential R code</summary>

```r
margin_plot <- function(lines) {
  ggplot(iris, aes(Sepal.Width, Sepal.Length, colour = Species)) +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~Species, nrow = 1) +
    theme(panel.margin = grid::unit(lines, "lines"))
}

animint(
  zero = margin_plot(0),
  one = margin_plot(1),
  two = margin_plot(2)
)
```

</details>
